verses.32:42: And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and called it Nobah, after his own name.
verses.33:1: These are the journeys of the children of Israel, who came forth from the land of Egypt according to their hosts, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.33:2: And Moses wrote down their departures according to their journeys at the command of the LORD; and these are their journeys according to their departures:
verses.33:3: They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the children of Israel went forth with an uplifted hand before the eyes of all the Egyptians.
verses.33:4: Now the Egyptians were burying every firstborn whom the LORD had struck down among them; upon their gods also the LORD had executed judgments.
verses.33:5: Then the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses and encamped at Succoth.
verses.33:6: They journeyed from Succoth and encamped at Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
verses.33:7: They journeyed from Etham and turned back to Pi Hahiroth, which faces Baal Zephon; and they encamped before Migdol.
verses.33:8: They journeyed from before Hahiroth and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness; and they went a journey of three days in the Wilderness of Etham and encamped at Marah.
verses.33:9: They journeyed from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they encamped there.
verses.33:10: They journeyed from Elim and encamped by the Red Sea.
verses.33:11: They journeyed from the Red Sea and encamped in the Wilderness of Sin.
verses.33:12: They journeyed from the Wilderness of Sin and encamped at Dophkah.
verses.33:13: They journeyed from Dophkah and encamped at Alush.
verses.33:14: They journeyed from Alush and encamped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.33:15: They journeyed from Rephidim and encamped in the Wilderness of Sinai.
verses.33:16: They journeyed from the Wilderness of Sinai and encamped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
verses.33:17: They journeyed from Kibroth Hattaavah and encamped at Hazeroth.
verses.33:18: They journeyed from Hazeroth and encamped at Rithmah.
verses.33:19: They journeyed from Rithmah and encamped at Rimmon Perez.
verses.33:20: They journeyed from Rimmon Perez and encamped at Libnah.
verses.33:21: They journeyed from Libnah and encamped at Rissah.
verses.33:22: They journeyed from Rissah and encamped at Kehelathah.
verses.33:23: They journeyed from Kehelathah and encamped at Mount Shepher.
verses.33:24: They journeyed from Mount Shepher and encamped at Haradah.
verses.33:25: They journeyed from Haradah and encamped at Makheloth.
verses.33:26: They journeyed from Makheloth and encamped at Tahath.
verses.33:27: They journeyed from Tahath and encamped at Terah.
verses.33:28: They journeyed from Terah and encamped at Mithkah.
verses.33:29: They journeyed from Mithkah and encamped at Hashmonah.
verses.33:30: They journeyed from Hashmonah and encamped at Moseroth.
verses.33:31: They journeyed from Moseroth and encamped at Bene Jaakan.
verses.33:32: They journeyed from Bene Jaakan and encamped at Hor Haggidgad.
verses.33:33: They journeyed from Hor Haggidgad and encamped at Jotbathah.
verses.33:34: They journeyed from Jotbathah and encamped at Abronah.
verses.33:35: They journeyed from Abronah and encamped at Ezion Geber.
verses.33:36: They journeyed from Ezion Geber and encamped in the Wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh.
verses.33:37: They journeyed from Kadesh and encamped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
verses.33:38: Then Aaron the priest ascended Mount Hor at the command of the LORD and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Israel came forth from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
verses.33:39: And Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
verses.33:40: Now the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the children of Israel.
verses.33:41: They journeyed from Mount Hor and encamped at Zalmonah.
verses.33:42: They journeyed from Zalmonah and encamped at Punon.
verses.33:43: They journeyed from Punon and encamped at Oboth.
verses.33:44: They journeyed from Oboth and encamped at Iye Abarim, on the border of Moab.
verses.33:45: They journeyed from Iyim and encamped at Dibon Gad.
verses.33:46: They journeyed from Dibon Gad and encamped at Almon Diblathaim.
verses.33:47: They journeyed from Almon Diblathaim and encamped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
verses.33:48: They journeyed from the mountains of Abarim and encamped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
verses.33:49: They encamped by the Jordan, from Beth Jeshimoth as far as Abel Shittim, in the plains of Moab.
verses.33:50: Now the LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
verses.33:51: "Speak to the children of Israel and say to them, 'When you cross over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.33:52: then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and you shall destroy all their carved stones, and destroy all their molten images, and demolish all their high places.
verses.33:53: And you shall take possession of the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.
verses.33:54: And you shall inherit the land by lot according to your families: to the larger you shall give a greater inheritance, and to the smaller you shall give a lesser inheritance; wherever the lot falls for each one, that shall belong to him. According to the tribes of your fathers you shall receive your inheritance.
verses.33:55: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then it shall come to pass that those of them whom you leave behind shall be barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they shall afflict you in the land in which you dwell.
verses.33:56: Moreover, it shall come to pass that as I purposed to do to them, so I will do to you.'"
verses.34:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:2: "Command the children of Israel, and say to them, 'When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that shall fall to you for an inheritance, the land of Canaan according to its borders:
verses.34:3: Your southern quarter shall be from the Wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom, and your southern border shall extend from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.
verses.34:4: Then your border shall turn southward of the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass on to Zin, and its limits shall reach southward of Kadesh Barnea; then it shall go forth to Hazar Addar and pass on to Azmon.
verses.34:5: From Azmon the border shall turn to the Brook of Egypt, and its limits shall reach to the sea.
verses.34:6: As for the western border, you shall have the Great Sea and its coastline; this shall be your western border.
verses.34:7: And this shall be your northern border: from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line to Mount Hor;
verses.34:8: from Mount Hor you shall mark out your line to the entrance of Hamath, and the limits of the border shall be at Zedad.
verses.34:9: Then the border shall go forth to Ziphron, and its limits shall be at Hazar Enan; this shall be your northern border.
verses.34:10: And you shall mark out your eastern border from Hazar Enan to Shepham;
verses.34:11: the border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; and the border shall descend and touch the eastern slope of the Sea of Chinnereth.
verses.34:12: Then the border shall go down along the Jordan, and its limits shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to its borders all around.'"
verses.34:13: So Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying, "This is the land which you shall inherit by lot, which the LORD has commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe.
verses.34:14: For the tribe of the children of the Reubenites according to the house of their fathers, and the tribe of the children of the Gadites according to the house of their fathers, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.
verses.34:15: The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise."
verses.34:16: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:17: "These are the names of the men who shall divide the land among you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.34:18: And you shall take one leader from every tribe to divide the land for the inheritance.
verses.34:19: These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh;
verses.34:20: from the tribe of the children of Simeon, Shemuel the son of Ammihud;
verses.34:21: from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon;
verses.34:22: a leader from the tribe of the children of Dan, Bukki the son of Jogli;
verses.34:23: from the children of Joseph: a leader from the tribe of the children of Manasseh, Hanniel the son of Ephod,
verses.34:24: and a leader from the tribe of the children of Ephraim, Kemuel the son of Shiphtan;
verses.34:25: a leader from the tribe of the children of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach;
verses.34:26: a leader from the tribe of the children of Issachar, Paltiel the son of Azzan;
verses.34:27: a leader from the tribe of the children of Asher, Ahihud the son of Shelomi;
verses.34:28: and a leader from the tribe of the children of Naphtali, Pedahel the son of Ammihud."
verses.34:29: These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to divide the inheritance to the children of Israel in the land of Canaan.
verses.35:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
verses.35:2: "Command the children of Israel that they give to the Levites from the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in, and you shall also give to the Levites pasturelands around the cities.
verses.35:3: The cities shall be theirs to dwell in, and their pasturelands shall be for their livestock, for their possessions, and for all their beasts.
verses.35:4: And the pasturelands of the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall extend from the wall of the city outward a thousand cubits all around.
verses.35:5: And you shall measure outside the city on the east side two thousand cubits, on the south side two thousand cubits, on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the midst; this shall belong to them as the pasturelands of the cities.
verses.35:6: Now among the cities which you shall give to the Levites, you shall appoint six cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee; and in addition to these you shall give forty-two cities.
verses.35:7: So all the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, both them and their pasturelands.
verses.35:8: And as for the cities which you shall give from the possession of the children of Israel, from the larger you shall give more, and from the smaller you shall give less; each shall give of its cities to the Levites according to the inheritance that it inherits."
verses.35:9: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.35:10: "Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, 'When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.35:11: then you shall appoint cities for yourselves to be cities of refuge for you, that the manslayer who kills any person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.35:12: And the cities shall be for you a refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer shall not die until he stands before the congregation in judgment.
verses.35:13: And of the cities which you give, there shall be six cities of refuge for you.
verses.35:14: You shall appoint three cities beyond the Jordan, and three cities you shall appoint in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
verses.35:15: For the children of Israel, and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them, these six cities shall be for refuge, that everyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.35:16: But if he strikes him with an instrument of iron, so that he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:17: And if he strikes him with a stone in the hand by which one may die, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:18: Or if he strikes him with a wooden instrument in the hand by which one may die, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:19: The avenger of blood himself shall put the murderer to death; when he meets him, he shall put him to death.
verses.35:20: And if he pushes him out of hatred, or throws something at him while lying in wait, so that he dies,
verses.35:21: or in enmity he strikes him with his hand, so that he dies, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death, for he is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when he meets him.
verses.35:22: However, if he pushes him suddenly without enmity, or throws any object upon him without lying in wait,
verses.35:23: or drops upon him any stone by which one may die, without seeing him, so that he dies, though he was not his enemy nor seeking his harm,
verses.35:24: then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.
verses.35:25: And the congregation shall deliver the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall return him to the city of his refuge to which he had fled; and he shall dwell in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
verses.35:26: But if the manslayer at any time goes outside the border of the city of his refuge to which he fled,
verses.35:27: and the avenger of blood finds him outside the border of the city of his refuge, and the avenger of blood slays the manslayer, he shall not be guilty of blood,
verses.35:28: because he should have dwelt in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest. But after the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return to the land of his possession.
verses.35:29: And these things shall be a statute of judgment to you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.35:30: Whoever kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death upon the testimony of witnesses; but one witness shall not testify against a person to put him to death.
verses.35:31: Moreover you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death, but he shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:32: And you shall take no ransom for him who has fled to the city of his refuge, that he should return to dwell in the land before the death of the priest.
verses.35:33: So you shall not pollute the land in which you are, for blood pollutes the land; and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it, except by the blood of him who shed it.
verses.35:34: Therefore do not defile the land in which you dwell, in the midst of which I dwell; for I, the LORD, dwell in the midst of the children of Israel.'"
verses.36:1: Then the heads of the fathers' houses of the family of the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from the families of the sons of Joseph, drew near and spoke before Moses and before the princes, the heads of the fathers' houses of the children of Israel.
verses.36:2: And they said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the children of Israel, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.
verses.36:3: Now if they become wives to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they belong; thus it will be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.
verses.36:4: And when the Jubilee arrives for the children of Israel, their inheritance will be joined to the inheritance of the tribe to which they belong, and from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers their inheritance will be removed."
verses.36:5: Then Moses commanded the children of Israel according to the word of the LORD, saying, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks what is right.
verses.36:6: This is the word which the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, 'Let them become wives to whoever is good in their eyes; only within the family of the tribe of their father shall they become wives.'
verses.36:7: Thus no inheritance of the children of Israel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for every one of the children of Israel shall hold fast to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
verses.36:8: And every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any of the tribes of the children of Israel shall become the wife of one from the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may each possess the inheritance of his fathers.
verses.36:9: So no inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another tribe, for each of the tribes of the children of Israel shall hold fast to its own inheritance."
verses.36:10: Just as the LORD commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad.
verses.36:11: For Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, became wives to the sons of their uncles.
verses.36:12: They became wives within the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
verses.36:13: These are the commandments and the judgments which the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.

notes.1:2: The Hebrew phrase rendered 'Take the sum' is literally 'lift up the head,' an idiom for conducting a census; 'head by head' is literally 'by their skulls.'
notes.1:16: Follows the Qere reading qeru'ei ('those summoned,' Qal passive participle of qara') rather than the Ketiv qeri'ei ('called' or 'renowned ones'), which conveys essentially the same sense of duly appointed representatives.
notes.1:18: The Hebrew Hithpael verb rendered 'declared their lineage' occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes formally enrolling oneself by ancestral descent.
notes.1:51: In priestly legislation, 'outsider' (zar) designates any unauthorized person outside the appointed Levitical or priestly order who encroaches upon the sanctuary or its furnishings.
notes.2:2: The Hebrew distinguishes between the standard (degel) of each three-tribe division and the smaller ensigns (otot) of the ancestral houses, all stationed at a reverent distance (minneged) surrounding the Tent of Meeting.
notes.2:3: Literally 'eastward, toward the place of sunrise,' a double directional phrase specifying the eastern side facing the sanctuary entrance.
notes.2:14: The Masoretic Text reads Reuel here, whereas Numbers 1:14, 7:42, 7:47, and 10:20 read Deuel, reflecting a common interchange between the visually similar Hebrew letters dalet and resh.
notes.2:17: The phrase 'every man in his place' translates the Hebrew idiom literally meaning 'each man at his hand,' indicating every division's assigned station on the march.
notes.3:3: The Hebrew phrase literally reads 'filled their hand,' a standard priestly idiom for ordination and consecration to sanctuary service.
notes.3:22: The three clan counts in verses 22, 28, and 34 sum to twenty-two thousand three hundred, while verse 39 states twenty-two thousand; traditional explanations view the summary as rounded or as excluding three hundred firstborn Levites who could not redeem other Israelite firstborn.
notes.3:39: The Masoretic Text marks the words 'and Aaron' with extraordinary scribal dots (puncta extraordinaria), reflecting an ancient textual note because the command in verse 15 was addressed to Moses alone.
notes.3:47: One gerah equaled one-twentieth of a sanctuary shekel; five shekels per head for the two hundred and seventy-three excess firstborn yields the one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels in verse 50.
notes.4:2: "Take a census of" translates the Hebrew idiom "lift up the head of," used for taking an official count of those eligible for duty.
notes.4:6: "fine leather" translates Hebrew "or tachash," an uncertain term denoting a durable hide or fine tanned leather, traditionally rendered "badger skins" or "porpoise skins."
notes.4:7: "the table of the Presence" literally translates Hebrew "shulchan hapanim" (traditionally "the table of showbread"), referring to the table that held the continual bread before the LORD.
notes.4:20: "even for a moment" renders Hebrew "kevala," literally "like a swallowing," expressing either the briefest instant of a glance or the covering up of the sacred objects.
notes.5:18: The Hebrew verb translated 'uncover' denotes loosening or unbinding a woman's hair as a sign of solemn exposure or distress.
notes.5:21: Literally, 'causes your thigh to fall and your belly to swell,' an expression describing severe physical affliction and loss of fertility.
notes.5:28: Literally, 'and shall be sown with seed,' an idiom meaning that she shall be able to conceive children.
notes.6:2: The Hebrew term Nazirite derives from a root meaning 'to separate' or 'to consecrate,' denoting one set apart by a solemn vow to the LORD.
notes.6:4: The Hebrew terms rendered 'seeds' and 'skins' refer to the smallest parts of the grape, underscoring total abstinence from every product of the vine.
notes.6:23: In this Hebrew text, the LORD's promise ('and they shall place My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them') stands here in verse twenty-three before the words of the priestly blessing, whereas standard Masoretic versification places it after the blessing as verse twenty-seven.
notes.7:3: Hebrew eglot tsav denotes covered or litter-style wagons suited for hauling the heavy components of the tabernacle.
notes.7:13: The unit "shekels" is supplied after "one hundred and thirty" from the following clause; "the shekel of the sanctuary" refers to the official standard weight kept at the sanctuary.
notes.7:14: Hebrew kaf (literally "palm") refers to a small, shallow incense pan or ladle; "ten of gold" signifies a weight of ten shekels of gold.
notes.7:19: The Masoretic Hebrew varies the opening of the offering formula across the first three days: "And his offering was" (7:13), "He presented as his offering" (7:19), and "His offering was" (7:25, 31, 37, 43).
notes.7:72: Hebrew expresses ordinals above ten with a cardinal construction—literally "on the day of eleven day" (and similarly in 7:78 for the twelfth day)—rendered idiomatically as "On the eleventh day."
notes.7:85: The total of two thousand four hundred shekels is the sum of twelve silver dishes at one hundred and thirty shekels each and twelve silver basins at seventy shekels each.
notes.7:89: Hebrew employs the rare Hithpael participle middabber ("speaking") to convey the solemn resonance of the divine voice speaking to Moses from above the mercy seat.
notes.8:7: Hebrew "mei chattat" literally means "water of sin offering," referring to the water used for ritual purification from sin.
notes.8:11: Hebrew "tenufah" denotes a ceremonial presentation or "wave offering" by which the Levites were dedicated to the service of the LORD.
notes.8:16: Hebrew "netunim netunim" is an emphatic doubling literally meaning "given, given," rendered here as "wholly given."
notes.8:24: Hebrew "litzvo tzava" literally means "to serve a tour of duty," using terminology of organized muster; the starting age of twenty-five here contrasts with thirty in Numbers 4:3, often understood as a five-year period of initial training.
notes.9:3: Hebrew "bein ha-arbayim" literally means "between the two evenings," referring to twilight between sunset and darkness.
notes.9:10: The Masoretic Text places an extraordinary scribal dot over the final letter of "rechoqah" ("distant"), an ancient textual mark traditionally associated with questions over what distance qualified as a far journey.
notes.9:16: The Masoretic Hebrew reads simply "the cloud covered it," without the words "by day" found in some ancient versions.
notes.9:18: Hebrew "al-pi YHWH" literally means "at the mouth of the LORD," an idiom for "at the command of the LORD."
notes.9:22: Hebrew "yamim" literally means "days," and is used idiomatically here to indicate a longer period or a full year.
notes.10:29: The Hebrew noun hoten, translated father-in-law, may modify either Reuel or Hobab and can also denote a male relative by marriage.
notes.10:34: In this critical Hebrew text, Moses' words concerning the ark appear in verses 34-35 before the notice of the cloud in verse 36, whereas traditional Masoretic versification places the cloud at verse 34 and the ark sayings at verses 35-36.
notes.11:3: Taberah means Burning in Hebrew, echoing the verb for the fire of the LORD that burned among the people.
notes.11:15: The Masoretic text unusually writes the second-person pronoun in the defective feminine form att alongside a masculine participle as Moses addresses the LORD in distress.
notes.11:25: The Hebrew phrase velo yasafu is ordinarily derived from yasaf, meaning they did not continue or do so again, though some ancient versions connect it to suf, meaning they did not cease.
notes.11:32: A homer was a large dry measure of volume, approximately five to six bushels or about two hundred twenty liters.
notes.11:34: Kibroth Hattaavah means Graves of Craving in Hebrew.
notes.12:1: The Hebrew verb "spoke" is feminine singular, indicating that Miriam took the lead in the complaint against Moses.
notes.12:6: Following the Masoretic accentuation, "the LORD" introduces the main clause rather than modifying "prophet," yielding "I, the LORD, make Myself known to him in a vision."
notes.12:10: The Hebrew term tzaraat denotes a serious skin affliction traditionally rendered "leprosy," which rendered a person ceremonially unclean.
notes.12:13: Moses' prayer consists of only five Hebrew words with a doubled particle of entreaty, conveying immediate urgency and compassion.
notes.13:16: Hoshea means "salvation," whereas Joshua incorporates the divine name and means "the LORD is salvation."
notes.13:22: The Hebrew verb "came" shifts to the singular, which traditional commentators associate specifically with Caleb, who later received Hebron as his inheritance.
notes.13:24: The name Eshcol means "cluster" in Hebrew, commemorating the large cluster of grapes cut from that valley.
notes.13:33: The Hebrew term "Nephilim" denotes towering figures or giants of renown, also mentioned in Genesis 6:4.
notes.14:9: The Hebrew idiom "they are our bread" signifies that the inhabitants will be easily overcome; "their protection" is literally "their shade."
notes.14:14: "Face to face" translates the Hebrew idiom literally meaning "eye to eye," denoting clear and visible presence.
notes.14:30: "Lifted up My hand" is the customary Hebrew idiom for swearing a solemn oath.
notes.14:36: Ketiv/Qere: the Qere reads the causative verb "caused ... to murmur" (translated here), while the Ketiv reads "murmured."
notes.15:4: The Hebrew dry measure issaron denotes one-tenth of an ephah (roughly two quarts), and the liquid measure hin equals roughly one gallon.
notes.15:20: The Hebrew term rendered dough refers specifically to coarse meal or a freshly mixed batch of dough, from which a cake was set apart as a sacred heave offering.
notes.15:30: The Hebrew idiom with a high hand signifies deliberate, defiant rebellion against the LORD, standing in sharp contrast to the unintentional errors addressed in verses twenty-two through twenty-nine.
notes.15:38: The tassels with a cord of blue-violet dye served as a visible reminder of covenant obedience; in verse thirty-nine, the verb rendered go seeking echoes the same Hebrew root used for spying out the land in chapters thirteen and fourteen.
notes.16:1: The Hebrew verb rendered "took" lacks a direct object marker, leaving scholars divided on whether Korah took Dathan, Abiram, and On as confederates or the verb idiomatically means he took initiative in rebellion.
notes.16:11: The Masoretic text preserves a ketiv/qere variant on the verb for murmuring; following the Qere (tallinu, Hiphil), the translation reads "you murmur," whereas the Ketiv reflects an alternative vocalization of the same root.
notes.16:24: The Hebrew uses the singular noun mishkan ("dwelling") for the collective encampment of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, echoing the term used for the tabernacle itself.
notes.16:30: The phrase "creates a new thing" renders the emphatic Hebrew cognate accusative "creates a creation," highlighting an unprecedented divine act; "Sheol" denotes the subterranean realm of the dead.
notes.17:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, chapter 17 begins with the aftermath of Korah's rebellion (verses 1-15), whereas most English Bibles place these verses at the end of chapter 16 (16:36-50) and number 17:16-28 as 17:1-13.
notes.17:17: The Hebrew noun matteh carries a double meaning of both "rod" and "tribe," creating an intentional wordplay between the wooden staffs and the twelve tribes they represent.
notes.17:25: "Sons of rebellion" is a literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom bene-meri, denoting persistently rebellious people.
notes.18:1: "Bear the iniquity of" denotes assuming legal accountability and liability for offenses connected with the sanctuary and the priestly office.
notes.18:2: The Hebrew text plays on the name Levi and the verb rendered "be joined," highlighting the Levites' assigned role as assistants attached to the Aaronic priests.
notes.18:8: The Hebrew noun rendered "by virtue of the anointing" can also signify an allotted share or perquisite granted to the priests.
notes.18:19: A "covenant of salt" signifies an enduring, incorruptible pledge, reflecting salt's ancient role as a preservative and emblem of lasting fellowship.
notes.19:9: "Water of purification" is literally "water of impurity," meaning water designated for removing ceremonial defilement; the rite is called a "sin offering" in the sense of a purification offering.
notes.19:12: Following the Masoretic punctuation, the purification rite is performed on both the third and seventh days, as detailed in verse nineteen, before cleanness is restored.
notes.19:17: "Living water" denotes fresh, flowing spring or stream water rather than standing water drawn from a cistern.
notes.20:13: Meribah means "Contention" or "Strife," reflecting the Hebrew verb translated "contended" in this verse.
notes.20:16: The Hebrew word for "angel" can also mean "messenger," the same term used in verse fourteen for the envoys Moses sent to Edom.
notes.20:17: The King's Highway was the ancient north-south trade route running through Transjordan along the highland plateau of Edom and Moab.
notes.21:3: Hormah means "Devoted to Destruction," echoing the Hebrew verb for "utterly destroyed" in verses two and three.
notes.21:9: The Hebrew phrase "serpent of bronze" employs a striking wordplay between the closely sounding words for "serpent" and "bronze."
notes.21:14: This brief poetic quotation from the otherwise unpreserved Book of the Wars of the LORD is syntactically fragmentary, and the precise location of Waheb in Suphah is uncertain.
notes.21:30: The Masoretic text places an extraordinary point over the final letter of the Hebrew relative word rendered "which reaches," marking a notable textual curiosity preserved in the manuscript tradition.
notes.21:32: The Masoretic ketiv reads "took possession of," whereas the qere (followed here) reads the causative form "drove out."
notes.22:5: "The River" refers to the Euphrates, and "the land of the children of his people" follows the Masoretic Hebrew literally.
notes.22:22: The Hebrew term rendered "adversary" is satan, denoting one who stands in opposition to block another's path.
notes.22:32: The rare Hebrew verb rendered "perverse" signifies a reckless, headlong, or contrary course.
notes.22:33: The Hebrew particle ordinarily meaning "perhaps" functions here as a negative conditional with the sense "unless" or "if not."
notes.23:7: The Hebrew word translated "oracle" is mashal, denoting a formal poetic pronouncement or prophetic discourse.
notes.23:10: "The fourth part of Israel" follows the traditional sense of the Masoretic Hebrew, possibly referring to one of the four divisions of Israel's camp, though some understand the rare noun to mean "dust cloud."
notes.23:20: "He has blessed" follows the Masoretic Hebrew vocalization, emphasizing that God Himself has pronounced an irrevocable blessing.
notes.23:23: The Hebrew preposition translated "against" may also be rendered "in" or "among," signifying either that divination cannot prevail against Israel or that it is absent from Israel.
notes.24:3: The rare Hebrew phrase shetum ha-ayin is traditionally understood as 'whose eye is opened' to prophetic vision, though some interpret the adjective as 'closed' or 'piercing.'
notes.24:17: The phrase 'sons of Sheth' may designate a Transjordanian people associated with Moab, or it may be read as 'sons of tumult' in parallel with Jeremiah 48:45.
notes.24:21: The Hebrew contains a deliberate wordplay between ha-Qeni ('the Kenites'), qinneka ('your nest'), and Qayin ('Kain') in verse 22.
notes.24:24: Kittim originally referred to Cyprus and its coastal settlements, and later came to signify western Mediterranean seafaring powers more broadly.
notes.25:4: The Hebrew verb hoqa ('hang up') denotes a form of public execution or exposure, such as impaling or hanging, carried out openly in daylight.
notes.25:8: The Hebrew text employs a striking sound-play between ha-qubbah ('the inner tent') and qobatah ('her belly').
notes.25:12: Literally 'My covenant, peace,' using apposition to define the enduring covenant of priestly harmony and favor bestowed upon Phinehas and his line.
notes.26:2: Hebrew literally reads "lift up the head of," an idiom for taking a census or tally.
notes.26:9: Following the Qere reading qeri'ei ("chosen men" or "representatives"); the Ketiv reads qeru'ei ("those summoned").
notes.26:10: Hebrew nes literally denotes a banner or signal, here used of a public warning sign to Israel.
notes.26:56: Hebrew al-pi haggoral literally means "by the mouth of the lot," an idiom denoting the decision or direction determined by casting lots.
notes.26:61: Hebrew esh-zarah literally reads "strange fire," referring to unauthorized fire not commanded by the LORD.
notes.27:14: The Hebrew phrase rendered "rebelled against My command" literally reads "rebelled against My mouth," forming a wordplay with "strife" and the place-name Meribah.
notes.27:20: The Hebrew term rendered "majesty" denotes splendor, dignity, and recognized authority conferred in part from Moses to Joshua.
notes.27:21: "The Urim" refers to the sacred means of discernment placed in the high priest's breastpiece of judgment to inquire of the LORD's will.
notes.27:23: Whereas the LORD commanded Moses to lay his hand in the singular upon Joshua in verse eighteen, Moses here lays both hands upon him in full commissioning.
notes.28:4: The phrase "at twilight" literally translates "between the two evenings," indicating the late afternoon period before dark.
notes.28:5: An ephah was a dry measure of approximately three-fifths of a bushel, and a hin was a liquid measure of approximately one gallon.
notes.28:7: "Strong drink" denotes an intoxicating fermented beverage poured out as a libation to the LORD within the sanctuary precincts.
notes.28:26: "At your Feast of Weeks" literally reads "in your weeks," designating the harvest festival held seven weeks after Passover, later called Pentecost.
notes.29:1: The Hebrew phrase yom teruah denotes a day of loud sounding or trumpet blasts, inaugurating the seventh month; the prohibition of laborious work here and in verses 12 and 35 is narrower than the ban on all work on the Day of Atonement in verse 7.
notes.29:3: Hebrew issaron literally means a tenth-measure, referring to one-tenth of an ephah as specified in Numbers 28:5.
notes.29:15: The Masoretic Text places an extraordinary scribal dot over the vav in the first occurrence of issaron here, flagging an ancient textual note on the repeated distributive term.
notes.29:19: The Masoretic Text reads plural their drink offerings here and plural its drink offerings in verse 31, in contrast to singular its drink offering on the other days of the seven-day feast.
notes.30:1: In the Masoretic Text this verse begins chapter 30, whereas many English Bibles place it as 29:40, shifting the verse numbering of the rest of chapter 30 by one.
notes.30:3: Hebrew issar refers to a binding pledge or self-imposed obligation of restraint; the verb rendered profane literally means to treat as common or violate.
notes.30:14: The idiom to afflict the soul refers to acts of self-denial such as fasting, using the same Hebrew expression found in 29:7 for the Day of Atonement.
notes.31:5: Hebrew 'thousands of Israel' denotes Israel's traditional tribal clans or military divisions. The rare verb rendered 'supplied' also appears in verse 16 in the idiom 'commit trespass.'
notes.31:10: Hebrew 'encampments' refers to circular or walled nomadic settlements characteristic of pastoral peoples such as the Midianites.
notes.31:23: Literally 'water for impurity,' referring to the ceremonial cleansing water mixed with the ashes of the red heifer prescribed in Numbers 19.
notes.31:28: The Hebrew noun rendered 'tribute' appears in the Hebrew Bible exclusively in this chapter, designating the fixed levy reserved for the LORD from the spoils of war.
notes.32:7: The Hebrew Qere reads a causative Hiphil form meaning "discourage" or "turn away," whereas the Ketiv reflects a Qal form of the same verb; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.32:14: The Hebrew noun translated "brood" occurs only here in the Old Testament and denotes an increase, succession, or offspring.
notes.32:38: The Hebrew phrase "their names being changed" explains why the Reubenites assigned new names to rebuilt towns that had borne pagan divine names such as Nebo and Baal Meon.
notes.32:41: Havvoth Jair means "Villages of Jair" or "Tent-villages of Jair."
notes.33:3: "With an uplifted hand" translates a Hebrew idiom expressing a bold, triumphant, and unopposed departure.
notes.33:8: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "from before Hahiroth" here without the initial "Pi" found in verse 7 ("Pi Hahiroth").
notes.33:48: "By the Jordan at Jericho" is literally "by the Jordan of Jericho," referring to the stretch of the Jordan River opposite Jericho.
notes.33:52: "Carved stones" translates a Hebrew term for stones engraved or figured with pagan religious imagery used in idolatrous worship.
notes.34:4: The Ketiv reads singular wehayah ("and it shall be"), whereas the Qere reads plural wehayu ("and they shall be") to agree with the plural noun totsa'otav ("its limits" or "its goings out").
notes.34:6: The "Great Sea" refers to the Mediterranean Sea; the Hebrew phrase "and border" denotes its coastline as Israel's western boundary.
notes.34:8: Hebrew levo Chamat ("the entrance of Hamath") may also be rendered as the proper place name Lebo Hamath, a northern landmark near the approach to the Beqa Valley.
notes.35:5: Measuring one thousand cubits outward from the city wall in every direction (v. 4) establishes an outer square perimeter of two thousand cubits on each side with the city at its center.
notes.35:6: The single Hebrew term rotseach is translated "manslayer" when referring to an unintentional or untried killer (vv. 6, 11-12, 25-28) and "murderer" when referring to a deliberate killer (vv. 16-21, 30-31).
notes.35:19: The "avenger of blood" (Hebrew go'el haddam) was the nearest kinsman-redeemer responsible for vindicating the blood of a slain family member.
notes.35:33: Hebrew yachanif ("pollutes" or "profanes") describes the grave moral defilement brought upon the land by unpunished bloodshed, for which only the murderer's blood provides atonement (yekuppar).
notes.36:4: Land sold during hardship returned to its ancestral family in the Year of Jubilee, as ordained in Leviticus 25, but land transferred permanently through marriage inheritance would not revert and would remain attached to the husband's tribe.
notes.36:5: Literally "at the mouth of the LORD," a Hebrew idiom denoting direct divine instruction spoken through Moses.
notes.36:11: The Hebrew noun translated "uncles" refers specifically to paternal uncles, the brothers of their father Zelophehad, ensuring the estate stayed within their paternal clan.
notes.36:13: Literally "by the Jordan of Jericho," referring to the stretch of the Jordan River opposite the city of Jericho on the Moabite side.
